{{nihongo|'''Iwato Wake Shrine'''|伊波止和気神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

'''Iwatowake Shrine''' (いわとわけじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|Q71707|qid=Q71707}}, {{ill|Ishikawa District, Fukushima|Q1155869|qid=Q1155869}}, {{ill|Furudono, Fukushima|Q1205868|qid=Q1205868}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai Shosha|ja|式内小社|simple|Shikinai Shosha|qid=Q134917287}}, and its former shrine rank was village shrine.

=== History ===
[[File:Sekisan Omotego.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{Center|Mount Sekisan (the mountain in the center of the photo; the former site is at its foot)}}]]

=== Overview ===
The date of founding is unknown, but a former site exists at the foot of Mount Sekisan in the Sekibe area of {{ill|Shirakawa, Fukushima|Q750587|qid=Q750587}}, Fukushima Prefecture. This area is close to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shirakawa Barrier}}, and nearby place names such as former gold mine sites, “{{ill|Iwaki-Kaneyama Station|Q11587877|qid=Q11587877|lt=Kanayama}},” and “Kogane River” remain. It is therefore thought that in ancient times the shrine functioned as a guardian deity of the checkpoint and the gold mines.<br />In earlier times the shrine appears to have prospered; during the {{ill|Ōwa|Q1324768|qid=Q1324768}} ({{ill|961|Q23881|qid=Q23881}}–{{ill|964|Q23951|qid=Q23951}}), there was a {{ill|horse field|Q24887670|qid=Q24887670}}, and {{ill|Yabusame|Q1886157|qid=Q1886157}} (mounted archery) was dedicated. During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was known as “Togakushi Daimyōjin.” Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}, it was ranked as a village shrine.

=== Divine rank ===
* {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 10 ({{ill|843|Q23469|qid=Q23469}}), 9th month, 5th day: Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, Merit Rank Nine (''{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|cs|Šoku Nihonkóki|de|Shoku Nihon Kōki|es|Shoku Nihon Kōki|ff|Shoku Nihon Kōki|fr|Shoku nihon kōki|ja|続日本後紀|ko|속일본후기|pt|Shoku Nihon Kōki|zh|續日本後紀|qid=Q1041301}}'')<ref name="承和">''Shoku Nihon Kōki'', Jōwa 10 (843), 9th month, day of Kanoe-Tora (5th) entry (see {{Harvnb|Shintō and Shrine Historical Source Compendium}}).</ref> — recorded as “Iwatowake Tenjin.”

=== Grounds ===
There is a massive stone called the “Kasa-ishi.” It is said to have originally been located in the Kyūryū River and was moved into the shrine grounds due to river course changes.
